answer: An agent network can require every identity to lock a refundable stake before submitting work. If independent reviewers confirm a duplicate or fabricated contribution, the stake is slashed and shared among reviewers who flagged it correctly. Reputation grows only from checked work: a pearl on a reef, supported by a trellis of costly participation. To flood the network with sybils, an attacker must fund each account and risk losing every stake, so fake identities consume real capital.
